One id in, the whole run out, one row per hop (steps
0-12). The id can be a tool-call request_id, a
front-door request id or the 32-hex trace id; it is
expanded to every request id and trace id through
three maps: APIM, the MCP audit and the tool-result
echo. Optional tokenIds: the uti values a caller sent,
for a call the gateway refused.

Log Analytics: 2-18 min after the event.
Red boxes mark the exceptions to the request-id join.
- Any one id finds the whole run: a tool-call request_id, a front-door request id or the trace id. The request_id echoed in the Foundry tool result
bridges the trace and the request ids.
- Four exceptions break the exact join: the guardrail (trace id only), Entra (token id, in its own workspace), the private server (no APIM row) and
Search and Cosmos DB (matched by time).
- Sentinel cannot see Entra sign-ins in this build, so a failed sign-in is read from Entra's own log. In production, switch the Entra ID connector on.
1. Each layer logs to its own table and carries the join key it has.
2. Everything lands in one Log Analytics workspace, except Entra's sign-in logs, which stay in their own.
3. KQL functions join the tables on those keys and expose one chain.
4. The workbook, Sentinel, the ops alerts and the Demo Console read the functions.
